claims.text: Large language models are widely used in decision-making.
The reliability of large language models in critical tasks like healthcare is not well-established.
Large language models learn to infer latent concepts during pretraining.
A prompt-response concept model explains how large language models generate responses.
Response uncertainty in large language models decreases as the prompt's informativeness increases.
Experimental results on real-world datasets validate the proposed prompt-response concept model.

evidence.description: We show that the uncertainty decreases as the prompt's informativeness increases, similar to epistemic uncertainty.
Our detailed experimental results on real-world datasets validate our proposed model.

methodologies.name: Prompt-Response Concept Model
methodologies.description: A theoretical and empirical framework modeling how LLMs generate responses by inferring latent concepts from input prompts.

limitations.text: Large language model reliability in critical tasks like healthcare is not well-established.
